chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the adornment of women with gold and silver, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for women to wear gold and silver jewelry in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility (juz') for women to wear jewelry made of gold and silver, with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirming no religious objection to this practice. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often contextualized within the broader principles of adornment, distinguishing it from the prohibition of gold for men, thereby affirming its status as a legitimate worldly beauty (zīnah) for women.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about ornamenting the women with the gold and the silver. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about women’s using gold and silver as ornaments. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
